scope: Primary-source research for a public NHS outpatient booking workload finder and editable JUNO pilot measurement plan. Public event counts are discovery inputs, not causal evidence or a current work queue.

company.name: Frontier Health
workflows: Referral processing, prerequisite checks and routing
company.workflowCaveat: These are company-stated capabilities. The homepage names EPR, PAS and e-RS integration and assisted, automated and hand-off operation; it does not establish integration availability at every trust.

companyGrowthSource.title: Deployment Strategist role published by Frontier on MMC's portfolio jobs board
companyGrowthSource.text: The role covers deployment scope, workflows, governance, integration and procurement, change management, adoption, measured impact and expansion within accounts.
companyGrowthSource.caveat: The listing was closed when reviewed; use as evidence of the stated deployment approach, not as a current open vacancy.

knownCustomer.name: East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust
knownCustomer.text: The trust's April 2026 board papers describe emergency-department collaboration with Frontier and JUNO, including diagnostic monitoring, bed availability and breach validation.
caveats: Use as an account-expansion discussion, not an uncontacted new prospect.
RXC East Sussex Healthcare is distinct from RYR University Hospitals Sussex.
The vendor case study concerns emergency-department workflows. Its time and capacity claims must not become outpatient cancellation-reduction assumptions.
No comprehensive customer register was found. Absence of a public case study does not prove a trust is not a customer.

avoidClaims: The team's prior work across more than 40 NHS trusts is not a JUNO customer count.
Do not apply the homepage's scheduling-time reduction claim to a new trust or assume an eight-week deployment guarantee.
Do not label historical HES activity as an addressable, unrebooked queue.

RWE.name: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust
RWE.suitability: Strong documented operational relevance; check incumbents and scope before approaching.

need.title: Late rebooking communication and administrative capacity
need.text: The outpatient DNA section reports PAS-to-Accurx feed problems, late cancellation/rebooking letters and limited administrative capacity to answer calls or action cancel/rebook requests. It also states that Accurx reminders are live in most services.
need.caveat: This is a reported outpatient DNA root-cause analysis, not an explanation of all hospital-cancelled first appointments in HES.

earlierNeed.text: The report describes admin shortages, reminder-feed issues and an automated booking/calling system being procured.
earlierNeed.caveat: The meeting date is 12 February despite the March URL path. Completion of this specific procurement has not been established.

incumbents.name: Accurx / Nervecentre PAS
incumbents.status: Operational reminders with reported integration issues
incumbents.text: The latest report says automated reminders are live in most services, including imaging and therapies.

incumbents.name: OTUA / OTTO
incumbents.status: Named in NHS plan; pilot and wider rollout reported by supplier
incumbents.text: The ICB 2025/26 operational plan names OTUA as an automated patient booking tool. OTUA describes an 18-week cardiology pilot at UHL and subsequent rollout across sites.
incumbents.caveat: Pilot effects and rollout status are supplier-reported; neither establishes the exact scope or award of February's booking/calling procurement.

incumbents.name: Dedalus
incumbents.status: Direct award recorded for imaging-related booking automation
incumbents.text: The government procurement notice names Dedalus for cloud automation aligned with UHL's imaging strategy and an NHS App appointment-booking gateway. It lists estimated contract dates 2 April 2026 to 1 April 2027.
incumbents.caveat: Government mirror verified; original FTS page could not be retrieved. This is an imaging-specific contract, not proof that the broader February procurement completed or that the system is fully deployed.

route.label: Health Innovation Hub — industry solution submission
route.text: Official innovation front door welcomes industry proposals and supports pilots, implementation and scale.

procurementRoute.label: UHL procurement mailbox published on the contract notice

RWE.nextQuestion: Which cancellation/rebooking queues remain manual after Accurx/PAS work, OTTO and imaging automation, and can we measure the remaining staff handling time?
RWE.dataContext: The build's extracted hospital-cancelled first-appointment total declined from 85,475 in 2024/25 to 80,540 in 2025/26. Describe substantial reported workload, not deterioration. Public operational evidence and HES counts are separate signals.

RX1.name: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust
RX1.suitability: Existing booking improvement programme; investigate complementary scope.

need.title: Booking-rule alignment and outpatient access
need.text: The trust says dermatology improved booking processes and aligned booking rules, creating more than 150 additional new outpatient appointments per month with benefits expected from June.
need.caveat: A dermatology improvement example, not evidence that all trust-level first cancellations originate in dermatology or that those processes remain manual.

existingProgramme.text: The trust's 2025 transformation announcement includes shorter first-outpatient waits, an app for booking/rescheduling, and improved diagnostic booking.

route.label: Research and Innovation — Industry and Contracts team
route.text: Official commercial team for industry research and adoption discussions; the page also offers nuhnt.commercialresearch@nhs.net for expressions of interest.
route.caveat: Research/industry entry point, not evidence of purchasing authority for outpatient operations.

RX1.nextQuestion: Which queues still require manual coordination after booking-rule alignment and app rollout, and which service owner could sponsor a measured workflow pilot?

RYJ.name: Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust
RYJ.suitability: Useful established pilot-design comparator; confirm unmet first-appointment scope.

need.title: Patient choice before follow-up booking
need.text: The trust describes a choice-booking pilot covering over 2,000 follow-up appointments in five services: a text to confirm need, telephone offers closer to the appointment, and a letter if contact fails.
need.caveat: This was a follow-up pilot, not the first-appointment population in the default HES view. Reported local improvements must not be used as assumed JUNO effects.

route.label: Paddington Life Sciences — commercial partnerships
route.text: The official NHS partnership site lists Dr Suki Balendra for commercial partnership enquiries.

RYJ.nextQuestion: Which first-appointment or exception-handling workflows remain outside the choice-booking process, and what would a complementary pilot measure?

RWD.name: United Lincolnshire Hospitals NHS Trust
RWD.suitability: Current programme context; avoid treating an active transformation as untouched scope.

need.title: Fragmented booking administration and patient contact
need.text: The trust describes its April 2026 Patient Services Hub replacing fragmented administration across 15 systems and 40 mailboxes. It says three-quarters of prior calls concerned checking, rebooking or cancelling appointments.
need.caveat: The same update reports automated self-service, SMS filling of short-notice slots and a six-month implementation pause announced in July. This is an active programme with implementation concerns, not evidence of available procurement.

route.label: Research and Innovation enquiries
route.caveat: A general research route only; a specific outpatient innovation or purchasing route was not verified.

RWD.nextQuestion: After the Patient Services Hub review, which exceptions still need staff coordination, and is a complementary measured pilot appropriate before further rollout?

facts: The publication describes appointments, not unique patients. A patient can have several first appointments across different care episodes.
HES outpatient coverage concerns activity in England. It includes private patients treated in NHS hospitals and NHS-funded independent-sector activity.
Some providers submit attended appointments only, so cancellation and DNA counts can understate activity. Low or zero reports are not evidence of no workflow.
For subnational counts, values 1–7 are suppressed as '*' or zero with a Y suppression flag. True zero is unchanged; other counts are rounded to the nearest five.
Totals calculated before rounding can differ from sums of rounded components. Derived app totals and run-rates should be labelled approximate.
The provider CSV does not supply the specialty-by-cancellation cross-tab needed to assign these provider totals to specialties.
designDecisions: Keep suppressed values unknown; never turn a suppression flag into a true zero.
Separate observed annual event counts from user-entered scope, handling time and eligibility assumptions.
A cancellation event is not necessarily one unique administrative job, one patient, or an unresolved task.
Annual count divided by 52 is a simple average run-rate, not a seasonal forecast or current backlog.
Treat prior-year changes as changes in reported activity; check reporting completeness and organisation changes before causal interpretation.
Do not conflate provider CSV measure codes 16/17, 06/07 and 11/12 with the metadata's different attendance-type code system.

existingTools.name: NHS Hospital Outpatient Activity provider dashboard
existingTools.text: The publication already includes an interactive provider tool using its provider open data.

existingTools.name: NHS Federated Data Platform outpatient product
existingTools.text: NHS already offers outpatient operational functionality, including clinic/room management and cancellation handling.

existingTools.name: NHS outpatient improvement guidance
existingTools.text: National operational guidance and existing NHS systems should inform local discovery, rather than assuming a missing dashboard.

proposedDistinctValue.label: Find a booking workflow, then produce a testable pilot scope
proposedDistinctValue.text: Connect public provider event volumes to a selected administrative workflow, incumbent-aware discovery questions, explicit local assumptions and an exportable measurement plan.
suggestedBaselineMeasures: Staff handling minutes per eligible event, using an agreed local definition
Contacts and attempts per completed rebooking
Time from cancellation/request to confirmed new appointment
Manual exception, escalation and unresolved-request rates
Booking accuracy, duplicate communication and accessible non-digital route availability
proposedDistinctValue.caveat: These are suggested evaluation measures, not outcomes demonstrated by public HES counts.
